title: Keel's mandate pairs demand-side distribution of USDS with supply-side allocation returns on Sky's collateral
content:
A.6.1.1.3.1 defines Keel as "an Agent dedicated to expanding access to USDS, sUSDS, and other Sky benefits with an initial focus on the Solana ecosystem," leveraging "strategic incentives and partnerships to foster adoption, deliver the Sky Savings Rate, and bring USDS liquidity to new markets."

The same paragraph then adds a second, structurally different mandate: Keel "also identifies and executes allocation opportunities to generate excess returns on assets in Sky's collateral portfolio."

These are not variations on one activity. The first is *distribution* — spending incentives to place USDS and the Sky Savings Rate in front of new users, which costs Sky money in the short run. The second is *asset management* — earning yield on collateral Sky already holds, which makes Sky money. Bundling them into one Agent means Keel's own P&L can offset the cost of distribution against the return on allocation, so growth spending does not have to be justified line-by-line against a separate revenue source.

It also means the Agent's risk profile is mixed: a distribution failure and an allocation loss both land on the same balance sheet, and the Agent's governance must arbitrate between two very different kinds of opportunity for the same capital and attention. The stated forward plan — "a user-facing DeFi hub as well as other products... including borrowing and lending solutions" — extends the same logic: Keel expects to own the venue where distribution and allocation meet.
description: One Agent carries two economically opposite jobs: growing USDS/sUSDS adoption in new markets, and generating excess returns on assets already held in Sky's collateral portfolio.
